lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Part 4. You will hear a lecture about kelp forests. You now have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Good morning. In today's lecture on marine ecosystems, I'm going to talk about kelp forests: what they are, why they matter, what's happening to them, and what's being done to protect them.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Let's start with what kelp actually is. Although it looks like a plant, kelp isn't a true plant at all. It's a type of large brown seaweed, and it grows in cold, shallow water along rocky coasts.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Kelp doesn't have roots. Instead, it has a structure called a holdfast, which grips onto rocks on the sea floor. That's why you won't find kelp growing on sand or mud: there's simply nothing for it to hold on to.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: And it grows remarkably fast. In good conditions, giant kelp can grow by up to sixty centimetres in a single day, which makes it one of the fastest-growing living things on Earth.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: So why do kelp forests matter? Well, first of all, they're home to a huge variety of wildlife. You've probably seen photographs of seals and sea otters among the kelp, and they certainly live there.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: But perhaps the most important role of a kelp forest is as a nursery. Young fish shelter among the long fronds until they're big enough to survive in the open sea, so the forests support fisheries far beyond the coast.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Kelp forests also protect the coast itself. The dense forests slow down waves before they reach the shore, which reduces erosion, especially during storms.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Like other seaweeds and plants, kelp also absorbs carbon dioxide as it grows, and scientists are currently trying to work out how much of that carbon is stored for the long term.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: And kelp is useful to us in more direct ways. A substance called alginate is taken from kelp and used to thicken all kinds of products, from toothpaste to ice cream. It's also used in special bandages for treating burns and other wounds.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Now let's turn to the threats. Pollution is part of the story, but the biggest single threat is temperature. Kelp needs cold water, which is rich in nutrients, and when the water becomes warmer, kelp grows poorly or dies.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Marine heatwaves, when the sea stays unusually warm for weeks or months, have become more frequent, and they can wipe out a kelp forest in a single season.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Another threat comes from changes in the food chain. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, sea otters were hunted for their fur until they almost disappeared from much of the North Pacific.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Sea otters feed on sea urchins, which are small, spiny animals that graze on kelp. Without the otters, the number of urchins increased enormously, and they ate their way through whole forests, leaving bare rock behind.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Activity on land also plays a part. When it rains, soil is washed into rivers and makes coastal water cloudy. But even more harmful is fertiliser from farms.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Once it reaches the sea, the fertiliser feeds tiny algae, which grow so thickly that they block the light the kelp needs.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Often, several of these threats arrive at once. Along the coast of northern California, more than ninety per cent of the bull kelp disappeared in the years after 2014.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: A long marine heatwave hit the region, and at the same time a disease killed millions of starfish, including the large sunflower starfish, which is one of the main predators of urchins. With fewer starfish, the urchins took over.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: So what can be done? In several places, teams of divers now remove urchins by hand, and in some areas the forests have started to grow back surprisingly quickly once the urchins are gone.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Other projects grow kelp themselves. Tiny young kelp is attached to ropes, and the ropes are hung in the sea until the kelp is big enough. Then it's moved to the damaged areas and fixed to the rocks there.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: Finally, we can't protect kelp forests without knowing how they're changing. Divers carry out regular surveys, counting urchins and measuring the kelp along fixed lines, but they can only cover small areas.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: To see the bigger picture, scientists use satellite images. These go back to the nineteen-eighties, so they show how the size of the forests has changed over about forty years.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: This kind of long-term record is extremely valuable, because it helps us tell the difference between natural ups and downs and lasting decline.

lines.speaker: LECTURER
lines.text: In next week's lecture, we'll look at seagrass meadows, which face many of the same threats. Thank you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That is the end of Part 4.

groups.instructions: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
groups.title: Kelp forests
lines: Description: kelp is a large brown seaweed, not a true plant
Description: a holdfast, not a root, fixes it to {31} on the sea floor
Description: giant kelp can grow by up to 60 cm in one day
Importance: the forests act as a nursery for young {32}
Importance: they reduce the force of {33} before they reach the shore
Importance: a substance from kelp is used in toothpaste, ice cream and {34} for wounds
Threats: kelp grows badly when the water {35} rises
Threats: after sea otters were hunted, {36} increased in number and ate the kelp
Threats: {37} washed off farmland causes algae to grow and block light
Threats: in northern California, over 90% of bull kelp was lost after a heatwave and a disease that killed {38}
Restoration: divers remove urchins by hand
Restoration: young kelp is grown on {39} in the sea and then moved to damaged areas

evidence.quote: a holdfast, which grips onto rocks on the sea floor

31.why: The holdfast grips onto rocks on the sea floor. Kelp cannot grow on sand or mud because there is nothing to hold.
31.trap: Sand and mud are mentioned too, but as places where kelp does NOT grow.

evidence.quote: Young fish shelter among the long fronds

pairs: act as a nursery for young
the most important role … is as a nursery. Young fish shelter
32.why: The lecturer says the most important role of a kelp forest is as a nursery, where young fish shelter.
32.trap: Seals and sea otters are mentioned first, but they are adult animals that live there, not the young animals in the nursery.

evidence.quote: The dense forests slow down waves before they reach the shore

33.why: Kelp forests slow down waves before they reach the shore, which protects the coast.

evidence.quote: It's also used in special bandages for treating burns and other wounds.

pairs: for treating burns and other wounds
34.why: Alginate from kelp is used in toothpaste, ice cream and also in special bandages for wounds.

evidence.quote: the biggest single threat is temperature

35.why: Kelp needs cold water, so when the temperature of the water rises, it grows poorly or dies.
35.trap: Pollution is mentioned first, but the lecturer says the biggest threat is temperature.

evidence.quote: the number of urchins increased enormously

pairs: the number of urchins increased enormously
ate their way through whole forests
36.why: Sea otters eat sea urchins. When the otters were hunted, the urchins increased and ate the kelp.
36.trap: Do not write 'otters': the otters were hunted and almost disappeared. It was the urchins that increased.

evidence.quote: even more harmful is fertiliser from farms

pairs: causes algae to grow and block light
feeds tiny algae, which grow so thickly that they block the light
37.why: Fertiliser from farms reaches the sea and feeds tiny algae, which block the light the kelp needs.
37.trap: Soil is also washed off the land, but it only makes the water cloudy. The notes say the substance makes algae grow, and that is fertiliser. Both spellings are accepted.

evidence.quote: a disease killed millions of starfish

38.why: In northern California a heatwave came at the same time as a disease that killed millions of starfish, which eat urchins.
38.trap: Urchins are mentioned in the same sentence, but they were not killed: with fewer starfish, they took over.

evidence.quote: Tiny young kelp is attached to ropes, and the ropes are hung in the sea

pairs: is grown on … in the sea
is attached to ropes, and the ropes are hung in the sea
39.why: Young kelp is attached to ropes in the sea, and when it is big enough it is moved to damaged areas.
39.trap: Rocks are mentioned at the end of the sentence, but that is where the kelp is fixed after it is moved, not where it grows first.

pairs: These go back to the nineteen-eighties
40.why: Satellite images go back to the 1980s, so they show how the size of the forests has changed.
40.trap: Divers' surveys are also used, but they only cover small areas. The images that show change since the 1980s come from satellites.
